summary: Harness block states effective (narrowed) fence on scoped ticks per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §2

per.section: 2. Harness block states the effective fence

edit.description: prependHarnessBlock (src/Prompt.ts:218) and RenderOptions: on a tick carrying assignedEntry, render entry.files ∪ phase.entryChannelPaths as the revert boundary and phase.writablePaths separately as the outer ceiling, per §2. Unscoped rendering stays byte-identical.
Thread assignedEntry: entry into the fanout renderPrompt call (~src/Dispatcher.ts:1014) so Prompt.ts can render the narrowed fence.
Rewrite the §"The <harness> block" worked example (docs/CHAIN-AUTHORING.md:733-753) to show the narrowed scoped-tick rendering instead of the collapsed one.

tests.asserts: a scoped tick's rendered <harness> block names entry.files ∪ entryChannelPaths as the commit-must-touch-exactly-these fence and phase.writablePaths as a separately-named outer ceiling; an unscoped tick's rendered prompt is byte-identical to today's collapsed rendering.

acceptance: A scoped tick's rendered prompt names exactly the fence the write guard (src/Dispatcher.ts runAfterCommitGates, ~L1141-1160) will enforce; an unscoped tick's prompt is byte-identical to 0.6.2.
notes: The write guard this must match is already implemented (spec/RELEASE-v0.4.md §5) — this entry only makes the pre-commit prompt truthful, no guard-logic change. <prior-attempt> retry feedback is unchanged.

summary: Mount-dead aborts immediately; loop/job run exit non-zero iff errored-and-nothing-shipped, per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §4

per.section: 4. Exit-code contract — the run never lies to CI

edit.description: Dispatcher.tick() chain-resolution-failure path (~L483-499) already yields TickOutcome.failed=true for the load/mount class (chain module cannot load, state root missing, declaration invalid) — give this class a distinguishable signal (new exit-code constant sibling to EX_TERMINAL_MISCONFIG at L372, or a TickOutcome field) so superviseLoop can tell it apart from other tick outcomes. superviseLoop (~L1718-1784) must abort the run on first mount-dead occurrence instead of logging-and-continuing to --max, mirroring the existing EX_TERMINAL_MISCONFIG fail-fast branch (~L1744-1764). Track per-run whether any tick shipped a commit and whether any tick errored, so the run's own outcome can report both.

tickExitCode (~L130-133) and the loop command's exit mapping (~L771-777, also governs job run per docs/CLI.md L94): implement the exit non-zero iff (>=1 tick errored AND 0 entries shipped) rule; empty-queue settle and partial-success-with-surfaced-errors both stay 0, with tick errors named in the completion summary. Update HELP_SUB tick/loop exit-code prose (~L199-220) to match.
Add bullets under [Unreleased] Added (run exit-code contract).

tests.asserts: superviseLoop aborts non-zero on first mount-dead tick instead of burning to maxTicks; a run with one errored tick and one shipped entry reports shipped>0 and errored>0.
an unloadable chain exits non-zero after one tick's worth of work; an empty-queue run exits 0; a run with one errored tick and one shipped entry exits 0 with the error named in the summary.
loop process boundary still exits correctly for the hibernation and --max cases per the revised contract.

acceptance: A run against an unloadable chain exits non-zero after one tick's worth of work; an empty-queue run exits 0; a run with one errored tick and one shipped entry exits 0 and its summary names the error.
notes: Tick-level agent failures (crash, gate revert) keep today's semantics — only the mount-dead class halts the run. Design of the new signal (exit code vs TickOutcome field) is build's call; must not collide with EX_TERMINAL_MISCONFIG=78 (Axis-C orphaned awake flags), a distinct failure class.

summary: Detect CJS-context chain-load failure and refuse with usage-shaped message per spec/RELEASE-v0.7.md §5

edit.description: loadChainModule (src/Dispatcher.ts:234-274): catch tsx module-context signature family (tsx 4.21 'Cannot use import statement outside a module'; tsx 4.23 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND with tsImport '?namespace' percent-encoded) and rethrow a distinguishable usage-shaped error naming "type": "module" as the fix, per §5. Non-matching errors pass through unchanged (no false positives).

Surface the usage-shaped CJS-context refusal as exit 2, consistent with other usage errors and with the EXIT-CODE-CONTRACT taxonomy this entry rides on top of. Underlying loader error stays available as debug/verbose detail, not the headline.

tests.asserts: loadChainModule against the two known tsx CJS-context signatures (4.21 and 4.23 shape) throws the usage-shaped refusal naming "type": "module"; a genuinely missing dependency's error passes through unchanged.
chain load in a CJS-context fixture prints the usage-shaped refusal and exits 2.

acceptance: Chain load in a CJS-context fixture (the npm init -y smoke shape, pre-fix) prints the usage-shaped refusal naming "type": "module" and exits 2; a genuinely missing dependency still surfaces as itself.
notes: Blocked on EXIT-CODE-CONTRACT: exit 2 must sit consistently alongside that entry's mount-dead/errored-vs-shipped taxonomy rather than being designed twice. Detection signature is the empirical tsx 4.21/4.23 family from the inbox finding (c11d96b fixed the two known fixture instances by adding type:module; this entry makes the failure legible generically, not just those two fixtures).
